digest.lead: Anthropic announced a major governance shift with the Long Term Benefit Trust, establishing new oversight structures for the company's development as AI capabilities advance.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code received gateway compatibility improvements and new project management commands, while the community continues building innovative coding agent tools.

stories.headline: Anthropic Establishes Long Term Benefit Trust for AI Governance
stories.summary: Anthropic announced the creation of the Long Term Benefit Trust, a new governance structure designed to ensure the company's AI development remains aligned with long-term public benefit [1]. The trust represents a significant shift in how AI companies approach oversight and accountability as capabilities continue to advance.
key_points: New governance framework focused on long-term benefit rather than short-term profits
Represents growing industry focus on AI safety and alignment structures
stories.impact: This affects AI researchers, policymakers, and organizations evaluating Anthropic's commitment to responsible AI development, potentially influencing how other AI companies structure their governance.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.126 Adds Gateway Compatibility and Project Purge Commands
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code update introduces support for Anthropic-compatible gateways through the `/model` picker, which now lists models from custom endpoints when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is configured [1]. The release also adds a new `claude project purge` command for comprehensive cleanup of project state including transcripts, tasks, and file history.
key_points: Gateway compatibility allows developers to use Claude Code with custom API endpoints
New purge command offers granular control with dry-run, interactive, and bypass options
stories.impact: This benefits enterprise developers using custom API gateways and teams needing better project state management, making Claude Code more flexible for varied deployment scenarios.

stories.headline: Pu.sh: Minimal Coding Agent Built in 400 Lines of Shell Script
stories.summary: A developer shared Pu.sh, a lightweight coding agent harness implemented in just 400 lines of shell script, demonstrating how AI coding assistants can be built with minimal tooling [1]. The project gained traction on Hacker News with 75 points and active discussion from the developer community.
key_points: Proves that effective coding agents don't require complex frameworks
Shows growing interest in lightweight, hackable AI development tools
stories.impact: This appeals to developers seeking simpler alternatives to complex AI frameworks and those interested in understanding the core mechanics of coding agents without abstraction layers.

sources.title: Show HN: Pu.sh – a full coding-agent harness in 400 lines of shell

stories.headline: Use claude project purge to clean up Claude Code project state
stories.summary: The new purge command removes all Claude Code artifacts for a project including transcripts, tasks, file history, and config entries. This is useful for cleaning up projects or starting fresh without manual file deletion.
actionable_steps: Run 'claude project purge [path]' to delete all Claude Code state for a project
Use '--dry-run' flag first to preview what will be deleted
Add '-y' or '--yes' to skip confirmation prompts, or '-i' for interactive mode

stories.headline: Set CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 to eliminate screen flickering
stories.summary: This environment variable enables flicker-free alt-screen rendering with virtualized scrollback in Claude Code v2.1.88+. It provides a smoother visual experience when Claude Code switches between screen modes during long coding sessions.
actionable_steps: Add 'export CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1' to your shell profile (.bashrc, .zshrc, etc.)
Restart your terminal or run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply the change
Launch Claude Code to verify flicker-free rendering is active

stories.headline: Use visual mode in Claude Code for text selection and editing
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports vim-style visual mode (v) and visual-line mode (V) for selecting and manipulating text. This enables more efficient text editing workflows similar to vim editors.
actionable_steps: Press 'v' to enter visual mode for character-by-character selection
Press 'V' to enter visual-line mode for line-by-line selection
Use standard vim operators on your selected text

stories.headline: Use `/team-onboarding` command to generate teammate ramp-up guides
stories.summary: Claude Code can automatically create onboarding documentation for new team members based on your local usage patterns. This saves time creating training materials and ensures consistency in how team members learn your workflows.
actionable_steps: Update to Claude Code v2.1.101 or later
Run the `/team-onboarding` command in your Claude Code interface
Review the generated ramp-up guide and customize as needed
Share the guide with new team members

stories.headline: Use `claude plugin prune` to clean up orphaned plugin dependencies
stories.summary: Auto-installed plugin dependencies can accumulate over time, taking up disk space. The prune command removes dependencies that are no longer needed by any installed plugins.
actionable_steps: Run `claude plugin prune` in your terminal
Alternatively, use `claude plugin uninstall --prune [plugin-name]` to uninstall a plugin and clean up its dependencies in one step
